title: Spin Polarization of a Two-Dimensional Electron Liquid
authors: G. A. Nikolaev, M. E. Sergeev, I. V. Kukushkin, A. V. Shchepetilnikov
abstract: We show experimentally that the longitudinal resistance of a strongly correlated two-dimensional electron system provides a direct quantitative measure of its spin polarization. Using electrically detected electron spin resonance as an independent calibration of the spin state, we establish a parameter-free relation between magnetotransport and spin polarization, enabling spin polarization to be reconstructed from transport measurements alone. The extracted spin polarization quantitatively explains the magnetic field and temperature dependence of the electrically detected spin-resonance signal and allows the magnetic state of the electron liquid to be mapped over a broad range of carrier densities and magnetic fields.
summary: The research demonstrates an experimental technique to quantify the spin polarization of a 2DES by analyzing its longitudinal resistance ($\delta R$) via electrically detected ESR. By establishing a parameter-free link between $\delta R$ and spin polarization, the authors successfully map the magnetic state of the electron liquid across varying densities and fields. This method offers a powerful tool for studying strongly correlated electronic phases.
main_problem: To establish a direct quantitative relationship between the longitudinal resistance ($\delta R$) of a strongly correlated two-dimensional electron system (2DES) and its equilibrium spin polarization ($\xi$).
main_result: The study successfully established a parameter-free relation showing that $\xi$ can be quantitatively reconstructed solely from magnetotransport measurements, reproducing the known temperature and magnetic field dependence of ESR signals.
method: Measurements combine electrical detection of Electron Spin Resonance (ESR) with standard magnetotransport measurements on high-mobility 2DESs. The key technique involves deriving relationships by assuming the signal change is governed by $\partial R / \partial \xi$.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Two-Dimensional Electron Liquid (2DES), studied in ZnO/MgZnO heterostructures, which exhibits strong electron correlations and spin polarization effects.
key_observables: Longitudinal Resistance ($\delta R$), ESR amplitude ($A(B, T)$), Spin Polarization ($\xi$), Critical Field ($B_c$).
important_parameters: Carrier densities ($n = 0.5 - 1.8 	imes 10^{11} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}$), Magnetic field ($B$), Temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the ESR signal is dominated by changes in spin polarization ($\partial R / \partial \xi$) rather than resonant heating, and that orbital coupling effects can be minimized or accounted for.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup comparing $\delta R$ vs $B_{||}$ at various frequencies; they show the increase of ESR amplitude as polarization approaches saturation ($B_{||}/B_c \simeq 1$), and present reconstructed spin-polarization maps ($\xi(B, n)$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the experimental setup using ESR detection. It then develops theoretical relationships linking $\delta R$ to $\xi$, ruling out alternative mechanisms like resonant heating. Finally, it applies these relations to map the spin polarization across different carrier densities and magnetic fields.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-invasive method to probe fundamental quantum properties (spin state) in condensed matter systems using only transport measurements, which is highly relevant for understanding correlated electron physics beyond simple band theory.
